observation.visible_scene: A close, fixed view of a small stream cascading through a narrow gap between two large rocks. The right rock is covered in green moss; translucent ice formations arch over and beside the water channel on the left and below. Red and orange autumn leaves lie scattered on the wet rock surfaces and on the ice. A thin vertical sheet of falling water pours through the gap into a dark, churning pool at the bottom center.
visible_changes: The falling water column is in continuous motion: its bright white streaks and the foam where it spills over the upper ice edge shift shape and position from frame to frame, indicating steady flow rather than a start or stop.
The dark pool beneath the cascade shows moving bubbles and ripples whose pattern changes across the frames, consistent with water churning on impact.
All solid elements remain fixed: the mossy rock, the ice arches, the protruding red leaf on the central rock, and the orange leaves on the left ice do not move relative to the frame edges.
No camera movement is evident; background and foreground objects hold constant pixel positions throughout the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: The flow rate is ongoing at both crop boundaries; whether it intensifies, diminishes, or stops outside this segment is unknown.
The upstream source feeding the cascade and the downstream continuation of the pool are not visible.
uncertain_details: The exact circulation direction of the ripples in the lower pool is hard to track frame-to-frame due to low contrast in the dark water.
Any minute leaf flutter, if present, is not distinguishable from the static appearance across these samples.
